title: The Histories
description: An inquiry into the Greco-Persian wars that digresses constantly into ethnography, rumour, and marvels. The founding text of history writing, and openly unreliable in places.

title: History of the Peloponnesian War
description: A participant's austere account of Athens and Sparta destroying each other. The Melian Dialogue remains the standard citation for realist power politics.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
description: A thousand years of Roman history that keeps asking how we know what we claim to know. Beard is more interested in citizenship and ordinary Romans than in emperors.

title: The Fall of Rome and the End of Civilization
description: Argues from archaeology — pottery, building, literacy — that Rome's end was a genuine material collapse rather than a peaceful transformation.

title: The Twelve Caesars
description: Biographies of Julius Caesar through Domitian, mixing administrative record with enthusiastic gossip. The source of most lurid imperial anecdotes.

title: Montaillou
description: The daily life of a Pyrenean village reconstructed from Inquisition interrogation records. Heresy trials turned into an unusually complete social history.

title: A Distant Mirror
description: The calamitous fourteenth century — plague, schism, and the Hundred Years' War — followed through the life of one French nobleman.

title: The Making of the Middle Ages
description: How Europe between 970 and 1215 developed the institutions and inner life that made it medieval rather than late antique.

title: The Guns of August
description: The first month of the First World War, showing how mobilization timetables and misread intentions removed everyone's choices.

title: The Sleepwalkers
description: Reconstructs 1914 as a shared failure of many governments rather than a German plan. Deliberately refuses to assign single blame.

title: Storm of Steel
description: A German officer's front-line diary of the Western Front, written without disillusionment. Unsettling precisely because it does not condemn.

title: The Second World War
description: A single-volume global military history that keeps the Pacific, Eastern, and Western theatres in one frame and stays close to individual experience.

title: Stalingrad
description: The 1942–43 battle reconstructed from Soviet and German archives opened after 1991, including letters never delivered.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich
description: A correspondent who reported from Berlin writes the Nazi state's history from captured documents. Dated in interpretation, unmatched as eyewitness synthesis.

title: If This Is a Man
description: A chemist's account of ten months in Auschwitz, written to describe rather than accuse. Its restraint is what gives it force.

title: Eichmann in Jerusalem
description: Trial reportage that introduced the banality of evil, arguing Eichmann was thoughtless rather than demonic. Still fiercely disputed.

title: Ordinary Men
description: How a reserve police battalion of middle-aged German civilians became mass shooters, reconstructed from post-war interrogations.

title: The Cold War: A New History
description: A compact synthesis of the whole confrontation by a historian with archival access on both sides.

title: Berlin 1961
description: The year Kennedy and Khrushchev brought Berlin to the brink and the wall went up, told almost hour by hour at its crisis points.

title: One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich
description: A single ordinary day in a Soviet labour camp, published inside the USSR during the thaw. Its power is in the smallness of the victories.

title: The Gulag Archipelago
description: The Soviet camp system documented from the author's imprisonment and hundreds of survivor accounts, smuggled out for publication.

title: Citizens: A Chronicle of the French Revolution
description: Argues the Revolution was violent from the start rather than derailed by the Terror. Narrative history with a deliberately revisionist thesis.

title: The Old Regime and the Revolution
description: Shows how much of the centralized French state the Revolution inherited rather than created. Written by someone who had watched a later revolution fail.

title: A People's Tragedy
description: The Russian Revolution from 1891 to 1924, following individual lives through famine, war, and Bolshevik consolidation.

title: The Black Jacobins
description: The Haitian Revolution and Toussaint L'Ouverture, written as both history and anticolonial argument. The first major account to treat it as a revolution of equal standing.

title: King Leopold's Ghost
description: The Congo Free State as a private extraction operation that killed millions, and the early campaign that exposed it.

title: Orientalism
description: Argues that Western scholarship on the East constructed the object it claimed to describe, and that this served rule. Foundational and much contested.

title: The Scramble for Africa
description: How European powers partitioned a continent between 1876 and 1912, told through the men who did it and thought it reasonable.

title: Late Victorian Holocausts
description: El Niño famines in India, China, and Brazil turned catastrophic by imperial market policy. Climate and politics treated as one causal system.

title: Long Walk to Freedom
description: Mandela's account of the ANC, the Rivonia trial, and twenty-seven years of imprisonment, much of it drafted on Robben Island.

title: Speak, Memory
description: A pre-revolutionary Russian childhood recovered in deliberately artificial, gorgeous prose. Nabokov treats memory as composition rather than record.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
description: Two years of hiding in an Amsterdam annexe, written by a teenager who did not survive. An ordinary adolescent diary in an unbearable setting.

title: Hunger of Memory
description: An essayist's account of how education carried him out of a Spanish-speaking household and away from his parents. Deliberately unwelcome conclusions.

title: Team of Rivals
description: Lincoln's cabinet, assembled from the men he defeated for the nomination. A study of political management as much as biography.

title: The Power Broker
description: Robert Moses reshaped New York for forty years without ever winning an election. The definitive account of unelected power.

title: The Years of Lyndon Johnson: The Passage of Power
description: Johnson from the humiliations of the vice presidency through the transition after Dallas. Caro's specialty is showing exactly how legislative power is applied.

title: The Double Helix
description: A candid, self-serving account of the race to DNA's structure. Notable for how badly it treats Rosalind Franklin, which later became the story.

title: Surely You're Joking, Mr Feynman!
description: Anecdotes from a physicist who enjoyed safecracking and bongo drums as much as quantum electrodynamics.

title: The Man Who Knew Infinity
description: Ramanujan's journey from a clerk's desk in Madras to Cambridge, and his collaboration with Hardy. A biography about how mathematical intuition is legitimised.

title: A Mind at Play
description: Claude Shannon, who founded information theory in a single 1948 paper and then largely lost interest in fame.

title: Einstein: His Life and Universe
description: Uses newly released letters to connect Einstein's physics, his politics, and a personal life he managed poorly.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
description: The woman whose cancer cells became the immortal HeLa line without her family's knowledge or benefit. Consent and race in medical research.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
description: Argues geography and available domesticates, not innate difference, explain which societies conquered others. Popular, influential, and heavily criticised by specialists.

title: The Silk Roads
description: World history recentred on Central Asia and the trade corridors between East and West, with Europe as periphery for most of it.

title: Postwar: A History of Europe Since 1945
description: Europe from the ruins to the EU, tracking both halves of the continent and the memory politics that followed 1989.
